title: VPC security safeguard: Terraform module for security groups, NACLs, private DNS, and egress policies
creator: Samir Patel
description: Build a composable Terraform module that captures Redwood's recommended VPC security posture for Private deployments. The module should provide opinionated, but configurable, primitives for security groups, network ACLs, private DNS forwarding/resolution for internal services, and policy-driven egress controls. It will be used by both on-prem deploys and VPC-hosted stack templates to enforce consistent guardrails and support safe upgrades and automated health checks.
background: Customers running Private deployments need a repeatable way to provision secure network boundaries that meet our enterprise compliance baseline. Existing stacks have ad-hoc security group and NACL configs across repos; this work consolidates best-practices into a single shared module with clear upgrade paths and runtime health checks. Prior art: ENG-62190 (secure-egress-dns-federation) and ENG-81290 (secure-pathways-terraform-module) contain design notes we should reconcile.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes inputs for: allowed egress CIDR list, egress allow-list by service tag, SG inbound rules by role (control-plane, runtime, monitoring), NACL templates for public/private subnets, and private DNS forwarding zones.
Module has documented defaults that implement Redwood's enterprise baseline (deny by default egress, explicit egress policy tiers: restricted, monitored, open) and can be overridden safely.
Automated Terraform plan/apply runs in our CI using example stacks for AWS VPC and an on-prem network emulator with zero destructive changes in dry-run.
Health-checks: cadence-based Terraform apply + a runtime health-check script that verifies SG rules, NACL state, and private DNS resolution are in expected state; script returns non-zero on drift.
Module includes upgrade migration guide with at least two non-trivial migration scenarios (NACL rule renumbering, egress tightening) and runnable steps that preserve connectivity during migration.
Module code reviewed and merged (PR link recorded), with positive security review and sign-off by security@redwood.com.
implementation_plan: Draft HLD consolidating settings from ENG-62190 and ENG-81290; define canonical inputs and naming conventions (2 days).
Prototype Terraform module with sub-modules: sg/, nacl/, dns/, egress/; keep minimal external providers (aws, local_exec for checks) (4 days).
Add example stacks: private-vpc-default, private-vpc-restricted, onprem-emulator; wire CI to run terraform init/plan (3 days).
Add health-check scripts (bash/python) that validate effective SG/NACL rules and DNS resolution from bastion host container (2 days).
Write upgrade/migration playbook and runbook; test migration in staging with traffic mirroring (2 days).
Merge, tag module (v1.0.0-infra), and publish docs + example templates (1 day).
tasks: HLD: capture requirements and map existing patterns
Define Terraform input schema and defaults
Implement sg/ submodule with role-based rule sets
Implement nacl/ submodule with idempotent rule ordering
Implement dns/ submodule for private hosted zones and conditional forwarding
Implement egress/ submodule with policy tier enforcement and logging integration
Create example stacks and CI pipelines
Add health-check tooling and CI checks
Write migration guide and run migrations in staging
risks: Tightening egress rules can break customers' integrations — mitigation: provide 'monitor' mode and gradual enforcement via canary stacks.
NACL rule ordering issues on AWS can cause transient connectivity loss during updates — mitigation: test renumbering strategy and prefer SG-centric designs for fine-grained control.
Private DNS forwarding may create circular dependencies in hybrid networks — mitigation: explicit zone ownership and TTL/forwarding timeout defaults + docs.
On-prem variability (different CNI or firewall appliances) may make single module insufficient — mitigation: provide adapter interfaces and vendor-specific extension points.
Long apply times for large rule sets could exceed CI timeouts — mitigation: break example applies into staged plans and increase CI timeouts for infra jobs.
testing_and_health_checks: Unit tests: terraform validate + tflint for module code
Integration: terraform apply in ephemeral AWS account with automated connectivity tests (SSH, API, DNS lookups)
Drift detection: cron-run health-check script that calls AWS APIs to compare expected vs actual rules and emits metric to Datadog
Canary enforcement: use 'monitor' mode to log blocked connections before switching to 'enforce'
Upgrade regression tests: simulate rule changes and verify no packet loss for control-plane traffic in staging
upgrade_strategy: Non-breaking defaults: new module defaults should be permissive or 'monitor' to avoid immediate disruption
Two-step migration: (1) deploy module in 'audit' mode to collect telemetry; (2) switch to 'enforce' after verifying logs and alerts
Automated rollback playbook if critical control-plane connectivity fails (use previous module tag and documented rollback steps)
Major changes use semantic versioning; breaking changes require a migration guide and at least one weekly-deployment window agreed with platform teams
